## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
`refresh_fingerprints` must stop overwriting digests for files the manifest already tracks. As written, refreshing after a hand edit records the edited content, and `verify` then accepts the tampered file.

## Changes
This pull request adds two functions to `app/integrity.py`: `refresh_fingerprints`, which re-hashes the named files into the manifest, and `register_new_files`, which adds only names the manifest does not list yet. It also adds `tests/test_integrity.py` with one test for each function.

## Critical
- app/integrity.py:17 — correctness — Keep existing digests in refresh_fingerprints — If `tracked.txt` has been hand-edited, `refresh_fingerprints(root, manifest, ["tracked.txt", "new.txt"])` replaces its recorded digest with the digest of the edited content, and `verify` then returns `True`. The PR body says "Existing fingerprints let verification detect hand-edited tracked files," but line 17 assigns `entries[name]` without checking whether `name` is already in the manifest. The only refresh test (`tests/test_integrity.py:12`) passes `tracked.txt` unchanged, so it cannot catch this. — Running the refresh command after adding files with the tracked names included hides earlier tampering, so the integrity manifest no longer protects those files. — Fix: Skip names already in `entries`, as `register_new_files` does at `app/integrity.py:24`, and extend `test_refresh_registers_new_files_and_keeps_unchanged_entries` to edit `tracked.txt` before refreshing.
